q: 1. The department head can extend the time upto ............% of initial contract duration.
explain: Administrative rules often limit the authority of a department head to approve time extensions to 25% of the original duration; beyond this, higher approval is usually required.

q: 2. Best option to avoid the undue pressure, cartels and collusion during bidding process is ............
explain: Electronic bidding (E-bidding) increases transparency and prevents physical cartels or collusion between bidders because the process is digitized and hidden until the deadline.

q: 3. Which is not the part of bidding documents ............
explain: While the Invitation for Bid (IFB) advertises the project, the 'Bidding Documents' usually refer to the technical and legal package (drawings, specs, contract) provided to the bidder.

q: 4. Which of the following is done first in procurement of consulting services .............
explain: Expression of Interest (EOI) is the first step to identify capable firms before shortlisting and requesting a formal proposal (RFP).

q: 5. The maximum amount of project cost after the price adjustment should not exceed .............
explain: Many local regulations cap the total price adjustment (escalation) at 15% of the original contract price.

q: 6. E.O.I. is compulsory for procurement of consulting services if work amount exceeds .............
explain: As per PPR 2064, public notification for EOI is mandatory for consulting services above 2 million (20 Lakhs).

q: 7. While procuring the consulting services, R.F.P. is extended to ..............
explain: In the procurement of consulting services, an Expression of Interest (EOI) is conducted first. The Request for Proposal (RFP) is then specifically issued only to those firms that have been shortlisted.

q: 8. The authority of variation order up to 25% of contract cost lies on ..............
explain: In accordance with Nepalese Public Procurement regulations, the Department Head (Chief) generally has the delegated authority to approve variations up to a certain percentage (25%).

q: 9. The authority of variation order above 25% of contract cost lies on ..............
explain: Major variations exceeding standard departmental limits (typically above 25%) require higher-level approval from the Council of Ministers (Cabinet).
